title: Filolial Mask
text: “This is probably a problem cropping up all over Melromarc. We’ve gotten reports from neighboring towns and villages too.”
Crocodile Guy explained as much, indeed.
“Did Ren not anticipate that this incident would happen, I wonder?”
“Who knows.”
“Let’s head to the scene.”
“Yeah. Rafumi-chan might show up, but let’s hurry and go put a stop to this.”

And so we hurried down from the carriage and rushed toward the scene, I say. When we arrived, there were what looked like rough-edged adventurers, or bandits, or maybe just outright thieves—hard to say exactly what to call these plunderers—but they were in the middle of an assault.
“Bwooiiiiii!?”
“Hahaha! Drag off the women and children, kill the men! Today’s gonna be fun, I can tell already!”
“What a good era to be alive in! Hahhaa!”
Ah, the country really was in a sorry state of chaos.
“Wow, straightforward bandits. But you know… come to think of it, the rumors about Takt sounded like similar charges.”
Indeed. Takt was the very picture of a bandit, through and through. A reincarnated murderer, truly. I intended to keep handing him the ending he deserved, over and over.
“This is a human village, but I have passed through here before.”
“They were foolish people who got swept up in Three Heroes Church propaganda, but it does feel wrong to abandon them all the same.”
Right as Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy were about to step in to help, a voice rang out.
“Hold it right there!”
“Ah? What’s this?”
The one who appeared at the sound of that voice was… the Queen. Her face was hidden behind a fan, but there was no mistaking her.
“Oh, the Queen’s here? Then maybe it’s fine. The kingdom’s soldiers should be on escort duty too—”
Father and the others were about to jump in to help, but standing nearby was… Fleon-chan. Oh? A new outfit? She was wearing a blazer.

“I have seen your wicked deeds clearly! Raiding villages, capturing and tormenting good, honest people—this Blazer Fleon has witnessed your evil acts with her own eyes! I absolutely cannot allow this to stand!”
“Ah?”
Father furrowed his brow as he listened to Fleon-chan’s grandiose introduction.

“Even if the Heroes were to forgive you, the spirits never would. As long as my eyes watch over this land, I shall protect the people from all evil, for their sake! That is my duty, as the embodiment of the people’s hopes!”
And there, following right after Fleon-chan, was the Queen. What in the world was she doing?
“A nation exists for its people, and the hopes of those people now… stand here!”
With a flourish she hurled her fan high into the sky, then raised a compact in her hand and cried out:
“Melromarc, Grooow Uuuuuup!”

Fwaaash! A flash of light burst from the compact—the very same effect Rival had created for Filo-tan and the others’ outfit-transformation compacts wrapped around the Queen, and her clothes began to change.
“Ahh!? Too bright!?”

And what emerged was… someone whose hair had shifted into a style resembling Fiancée’s, wearing something blazer-like, looking to be in her twenties—but upon closer inspection, it was the Queen, striking a dramatic pose as she revealed herself.
“Blazer Milly, descending upon this place. In place of the Hero, it is now time for your punishment!”
A sparkling “kiiira-kiira-KIIIN!” sound effect rang out across the battlefield.
“This is your final warning. Surrender now, and I shall see your charges reduced.”
“Hah! Punishment, my foot! You’re a weird one, but you really think you can beat this many of us?!”
“If it were one of those so-called Legendary Heroes, sure, but there’s no way we lose to some bizarre nobody like you! Come on!”
“Dunno what’s going on, but she’s got a pretty good face on her. Heh heh, today’s looking fun after all.”
The bandits swarmed, closing in on the Queen—who called herself Blazer Milly—and Fleon-chan.
“If you don’t wanna get hurt, just shut up and take it quietly, you hear me?!”
Just as the bandit lunged at the Queen, she pulled off a beautifully executed kick against him.
“Milly! Kick! And then… Tiara Strike!”
She spun the tiara atop her head at high speed with magic and hurled it into the stomach of a bandit standing some distance away.
“Guhaaah!?”
“Damn! This one moves better than I expected. Oi! How long are you gonna keep rolling around?!”
“I-it hurts… m-my stomach, what the hell is this?! It’s digging in, it huuurts!”
The bandit struck by the Queen’s spinning tiara kept writhing where he’d fallen.
“Now, now, don’t go forgetting about me! Fleon, Kiiick!”
Spinning round and round, Fleon-chan leapt up, as if using some invisible foothold midair, then came crashing down at a speed better described as falling than descending.
“Whoa!”
“Ah, I missed.”
BOOOOM! The shockwave from Fleon-chan’s kick blasted the trees behind her clean away.
“Aahh!?”
The bandit who’d narrowly dodged that blast had gone pale in the face.
“Well, maybe this counts as overkill… Fleon-chan. Though the Queen seems pretty capable too…”
And so, from a considerable distance, we watched the scene unfold.
“…Should we step in to help, I wonder?”
“The mood suggests we should, but…”
There was, somehow, an atmosphere that made it hard to butt in.
“Oi! What are you all standing around scared for?! There’s obviously some trick to this! Just surround them and take them down already!”

The one who seemed to be the bandit boss barked orders at his underlings, clearly failing to grasp the situation. Sure, some of the men had lost their nerve, but with their sheer numbers, they figured they still had the advantage. It did seem to be a fairly sizable bandit gang.
“She’s pretty skilled, I’ll admit, but we’ve got our own trump card too, you know!”

With that, the Queen and Fleon-chan found themselves surrounded. From among the bandits, one man stepped forward with obvious confidence, as if he had some real skill to back it up, and squared off against the Queen and Fleon-chan.
“Teacher! Go ahead and take care of it!”
“Right on! Well, once we catch ’em, I get first pick, mind you.”
“Of course, of course!”

Licking his lips, the strongest of them seemed to be leading the charge while the rest tried to overwhelm through numbers—but then, right as someone tried to strike the Queen and Fleon-chan from behind: THUNK! Fleon-chan’s feather came flying in and blocked the attack.
“The hell?! There’s someone else out there too! Get out here, whoever you are!”
“Fuh.”
Stepping out from the shadow of a nearby building was a figure in a tailcoat, wearing a Filolial-sama mask. Who on earth was that?

“To unite as one and accomplish a goal—at times, that can be a most satisfying task, from the perspective of one who commands. But when that unity is used to commit evil deeds that make people weep and grieve, the matter changes entirely. Even in times of crisis for the world, perhaps it is fate that the seeds of evil should bloom into flower. But no matter how alluring that flower may be, it is, in the end, nothing more than a roadside weed—forever falling short of a true, shining brilliance.”
What on earth was he talking about? Some kind of half-baked poetic nonsense, honestly. Even the surrounding onlookers tilted their heads in confusion.
“Filolial Mask-sama!”
The Queen turned toward the one who’d come to their aid and broke into a smile.

“No matter how many gather, if the one commanding them lacks ability, all they can conceive of is a shallow, low-grade ambush, unable to see the whole field. That, people call a mob without order. When there is another watching from elsewhere, such an attempt becomes child’s play.”
“Guh—”
The one attempting the ambush collapsed. It seemed he’d been struck down by magic fired from his own shadow underfoot.
“Now, Blazer Milly!”
“Right!”
In a flash, the Queen produced a flashy rod from somewhere at her hip and took a stance—then the tip of the rod began to glow.
“Oi! We’ll stop that spell before it lands! Haaah!”
“Hmph.”
And then, this so-called Filolial Mask drew out what looked like a conductor’s baton and, with a flick, slowed the speed of everyone nearby—no wait, this was the Down spell that Itsuki uses!
“Al Liberation Down!”
Every last bandit in the area had their abilities lowered.
“Wha— these guys— they’re fast—”
No, you’re just slow now. Meanwhile, the Queen pointed her flashily glowing rod at the bandits’ bodyguard and the one who seemed to be their leader, and shouted:
“Rise Up, Melromaaarc, Illuminaaatiooon!!!”
With a great rumble, a mass of glowing purple ice burst forth and sent the bandits flying with tremendous force.
“Gyaaaaaah!?”
On top of that, in the middle of an even flashier follow-up attack, Trash’s signature light-refraction spell shot through the ice mass and pierced straight through the rest of the bandits.
“Gahh—”
“Uuugh…”
“Wh-what the hell are these people…”
Quite right. Indeed.
